Entertainment.title: JW Anderson x UNIQLO Turns Fall/Winter 2026 Into a Campus Drama
Entertainment.text: SummaryUNIQLO and JW ANDERSON’s Fall/Winter 2026 collection draws on theater, academia and spontaneous artistic expressionCropped silhouettes lead the outerwear, including a genderless Short Blouson and a women’s Padded Short JacketLambswool Fair Isle knits, flannel shirting and wool cashmere accessories bring vintage detailing into everyday wearUNIQLO and JW Anderson have unveiled their Fall/Winter 2026 collection, a season rooted in the worlds of theater and academic culture. Announced in New York, the lineup pairs vintage-inspired details with practical function across 13 womenswear pieces, 12 menswear pieces and four accessories. The result reads like a well-worn campus wardrobe, sharpened with modern proportions and cold-weather performance.Outerwear sets the tone, with shortened lengths running through the season’s key jackets. The genderless Short Blouson pairs a cropped body with a relaxed silhouette for a contemporary take on a classic zip-up, shown here in a deep burgundy with a gathered hem and cuffs. For women, the Padded Short Jacket delivers soft, generous padding in a boxy charcoal shape finished with oversized flap pockets, blending volume with everyday practicality.Layering pieces round out the cold-weather offering. Men get a Windproof Fleece Jacket, while women receive a Fleece Short Blouson, both designed around a comfortable fit that slips easily under or over other garments. The women’s Pleated Skirt adds movement to the mix through an asymmetric cut, offering a dressier counterpoint to the collection’s utilitarian outerwear.Knitwear carries much of the collection’s academic character. The Lambswool Fair Isle Crew Neck Sweater wraps an oatmeal base in red and pale blue motifs, while V-neck sweaters and crew neck vests arrive in an array of colorways and bold patterns. Underneath, the Flannel Boxy Shirt works a cream-and-black check into a cropped, open-collar shape, and the Straight Work Pants and faded, distressed Straight Jeans anchor the looks with relaxed, straight-leg cuts.Anderson framed the season as a meeting point between the stage and the classroom. “This season reflects the worldview of theater and academic culture, the intersections of unbound creativity. Building on traditional styles, we’ve created a collection that incorporates colors, patterns, and functionality to be enjoyed in a range of everyday settings,” Jonathan Anderson said in a statement.Accessories finish the uniform with the same varsity spirit. A ribbed Wool Cashmere Beanie in forest green and a navy Wool Cashmere Stole striped in red and light blue lead the cold-weather extras, joined by a navy Shoulder Bag. HEATTECH Socks complete the set in argyle, stripes and two-tone colorblocking, giving even the smallest pieces in the lineup a dose of pattern.The JW ANDERSON x UNIQLO Fall/Winter 2026 collection drops October 15, with the full lineup available at 15 UNIQLO stores in the US and online.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: A24’s ‘The Encyclopedia of Movie Cats’ Catalogs More Than 1,000 Felines Across Film History
Entertainment.text: SummaryA24 has published a 420-page reference book dedicated entirely to cats that have appeared on screenEntries run alphabetically and cover everything from famous characters to uncredited extras and real-life animal actorsOriginal essays and spotlight entries group felines by the roles they tend to play in cinemaA24 has unveiled The Encyclopedia of Movie Cats, a hardcover reference guide documenting more than 1,000 cats that have appeared in film. Organized from A to Z, the book treats screen felines as a cast in their own right, cataloging marquee characters and fleeting cameos with equal care.The premise starts with range. Across film history, cats have been cast as companions, antagonists and partners in crime, and have turned up aboard spacecraft, dressed in people’s clothes, named as heirs to fortunes and even transformed into half-human creatures. The encyclopedia argues that few animals have been handed such a wide spread of parts, and sets out to track all of them.That scope shows in who gets an entry. Household names like Puss in Boots and Mr. Bigglesworth sit alongside Holly Golightly’s orange tabby and Jones from the Alien franchise, but the book gives just as much attention to the anonymous strays and skittish cats that dart through a single scene. It also reaches back into myth and folklore, featuring the messengers of the goddess Bastet and witches’ familiars, and profiles real working cat actors whose credits are long enough to fill an IMDb page.Navigation follows a strict alphabetical order. The entries open with Abby Barnes’ Cat from The Truth About Cats & Dogs (1996) and close with the Zip-A-Tone Kitten from Zip-Tone-Cat-Tune (1972). Woven between them are original essays sorting felines into recurring screen archetypes, including Bad Omen Cats, Cat Lady Cats and Talking Cats, plus highlighted entries that map out individual feline filmographies and the most notable cats in cinema.A24’s physical build matches the reference-book ambitions. The encyclopedia is bound in a buckram-wrapped hardcover, runs to 420 pages and measures 7.75 x 10.25 inches, with more than 1,900 film stills illustrating the entries throughout.The Encyclopedia of Movie Cats is available to order now via the A24 Shop and ships by October 23.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Two Hong Kong Icons, One Case File: TEAM WANG design x CLOT Is Here
Entertainment.text: SummaryTEAM WANG design and CLOT have joined forces for “ON MY WAY,” a debut collaboration rooted in Hong Kong as the shared starting point for Jackson Wang and Edison ChenThe collection is organized around CASE NO.852, an archive-inspired design system named after Hong Kong’s international dialing codeThe limited lineup covers portrait T-shirts, Logo T-shirts, a Tang-style jacket, portrait masks and mugsTEAM WANG design and CLOT have unveiled "ON MY WAY,” the first collaboration between the labels led by Jackson Wang and Edison Chen. Built on a case-file aesthetic dubbed "CASE NO.852," the limited collection treats both founders, both brands and every individual piece as entries in a single archive. Its “ON MY WAY” guiding concept frames the partnership as two creative journeys that began in Hong Kong, split across different eras and disciplines, and have now converged.The design backbone of the collection borrows from old dossiers and personnel records, reworking portraits, names, biographical details, file numbers and traceability data into a graphic system of its own. At its center sits the number 852, Hong Kong’s international calling code, which functions as a master ID connecting the two founders, the two labels and each product. The effect is a capsule where every garment and object reads like a logged record, catalogued under one shared file.That approach is most literal on the portrait T-shirts, which carry black-and-white images of Wang and Chen alongside their names, personal details and CASE NO.852 identification codes. Rather than straightforward fan merch, the tees present each founder as a documented subject, matching the rest of the archival language running through the line.The Logo T-shirts extend the same system with archive numbering, the 852 marker, eyelet hardware and a strict black-and-white palette. They also pull design cues from two existing TEAM WANG design series, “SPARKLES” and “Invisible Man,” folding TWD’s own back catalog into the record. The name itself plays on cohesion and the sense of being on the same squad, a nod to how the partnership bridges the cultural backgrounds of both camps. Those details carry over to the Tang-style jacket, portrait masks and mugs, pushing the capsule beyond apparel into lifestyle goods, all released in limited quantities.The portrait masks double as the centerpiece of the “ON MY WAY” campaign, which casts skaters, dancers, DJs, photographers, designers and young entrepreneurs as its faces. Slipping on a mask of Wang or Chen lets each participant briefly adopt the restless, searching mindset both founders had early in their careers; taking it off returns them to their own unfinished chapters, whether a career pivot, an ongoing creative project or a period of uncertainty. The concept leans into the idea that growth rarely follows a straight line, and that nobody has every answer worked out.Before the official reveal, Wang and Chen opened the concept up to the public through an interactive online campaign tied to Chen’s return to Hong Kong, unlocking the collection once collective support hit 100%. The pairing itself reflects two brands at different stages. CLOT, which Chen founded in 2003, has spent more than two decades helping put Chinese streetwear on the global map through collaborations with names including adidas, Nike, Supreme, sacai and fragment design. Shanghai-based TEAM WANG design, co-founded by Wang and CEO Henry Cheung, represents a newer generation still expanding its aesthetic and international reach, giving “TEAM CLOT” the feel of a meeting point between an established institution and a label in motion.The TEAM WANG design x CLOT “ON MY WAY” collection is available via the TEAM WANG design Tmall flagship store, WeChat Mini Program and the TEAM WANG design official webstore, the CLOT Tmall flagship store, the JUICE WeChat Mini Program and the JUICE webstore. It will also be available in-store at JUICE locations in Shanghai, Shenyang, K11 Art Mall Tsim Sha Tsui, Causeway Bay, Taipei and Taichung.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Seth Rogen’s Houseplant x Droplet “Scent Burner” Suspends Hand-Blown Amber Glass Over a Tealight
Entertainment.text: SummaryHouseplant and Droplet have reworked Droplet’s cult-favorite Scent Burner as a special-edition piece built around The House ScentA custom hand-blown amber glass vessel hangs within a solid brass frame, warming fragrance oil and water above a tealightThe set includes the burner, The House Scent Fragrance Oil and eight tealight candlesHouseplant and Droplet have released The Houseplant Scent Burner, a special-edition take on one of Droplet’s best-known designs that reframes Houseplant’s signature fragrance as something to be heated rather than sprayed or diffused. The piece pairs a hand-blown amber glass vessel with a solid brass frame, turning the act of scenting a room into a slow, flame-lit process.The burner marks the third chapter in the partnership between Seth Rogen’s lifestyle company and the modern British fragrance house. The two first came together on an incense collection, then followed it with The House Scent Reed Diffuser. This time, they’ve turned to the Scent Burner, a Droplet signature that has built a loyal following for its unconventional mix of fragrance and form. “What excites us about this collaboration is that it goes beyond giving the burner a new look; it creates a completely different way to experience The House Scent,” said Droplet co-founders Sam and Lucie Beecham.The construction is what sets it apart. A custom amber glass vessel, blown by hand, sits suspended inside a frame of solid brass, with a tealight placed directly beneath it. The open structure keeps the flame, the glass and the frame all on display, so the piece reads as a sculptural object on a shelf even when it isn’t lit.In use, the mechanics are simple and analog. Users add 5 to 10 drops of The House Scent Fragrance Oil to water in the glass, and the tealight gently warms the mixture from below. Rather than releasing scent all at once, the heat lets the fragrance build gradually and spread through the space, with the flickering flame adding a layer of ambient light.The fragrance itself was developed by Rogen in Grasse, France. The House Scent opens with bright pink pepper and soft peony, then settles into warm santal and rich pine, balancing spice and florals against a creamy, woody base. Warmed in the burner, the blend becomes fuller and more enveloping than in its other formats. For Rogen, the appeal lies in the routine around it. “What really spoke to us was the ritual of it, lighting the candle, dropping our signature scent (developed in Grasse, France) into the vessel, and waiting for the smells to fill the room,” he said.Each special-edition set comes ready to use, packaging the burner with a bottle of The House Scent Fragrance Oil and eight tealight candles.Houseplant by Droplet – The Scent Burner is available now via The Droplet in the UK, and via Houseplant and The Droplet in the US.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: A 'Naruto x Ninku' Limited Anime Series Is Officially Happening
Entertainment.text: SummaryThe “NARUTO: What’s Next?” panel at New York Comic Con 2026 unveiled a 'Naruto x Ninku' TV anime limited series with a teaser trailer and key visualNoriyuki Abe directs the crossover at Studio Pierrot, with Tetsuya Nishio handling both character design and chief animation directionKishimoto’s new Naruto Shadow Rising manga arrived with a super teaser trailer, alongside a multi-year franchise roadmap called PROJECT RASENGANStudio Pierrot’s Naruto x Ninku anime limited series was officially announced at the “NARUTO: What’s Next?” panel during New York Comic Con 2026, pairing Masashi Kishimoto’s ninja saga with the world of Ninku across four episodes. A teaser trailer and key visual accompanied the reveal, and the creators of both manga are supervising the production. The same panel also confirmed Naruto Shadow Rising, an all-new manga drawn by Kishimoto himself.Noriyuki Abe takes the director’s chair for the crossover, a fitting choice given that he also directed the original Ninku TV anime at Pierrot in the mid-1990s. Kishimoto shares supervising duties with Ninku creator Koji Kiriyama giving the project direct oversight from the two authors whose work it merges. Nozomi Fukui supports Abe as assistant director, while Hinatasho holds the story credit.Tetsuya Nishio carries the heaviest visual load on the production, serving as both chief animation director and character designer. Consolidating those two roles under one artist means the task of reconciling two distinct manga art styles into a single cohesive look rests largely with him. Nishio also designed the characters for the original Naruto TV anime, which gives him a long working history with Team 7.The score is split across a three-way credit of Yasuharu Takanashi, -Yaiba- and Yusuke Honma, effectively blending each franchise’s musical lineage. Takanashi and -Yaiba- previously composed for Naruto Shippuden, while Honma scored the original Ninku anime. The four-episode runtime marks the series as a contained event rather than an ongoing broadcast.On the publishing front, Naruto Shadow Rising was introduced through a super teaser trailer, though the panel held back plot details, characters and a serialization date. Kishimoto drawing the series personally makes it his most hands-on Naruto manga project announced since the original run concluded, and more information is slated for the franchise’s Jump Festa 2027 panel.Both projects sit within PROJECT RASENGAN, a newly revealed roadmap outlining the franchise’s longer-range plans across manga, anime, trading cards and games, with teased projects extending into 2029. By the end of the panel, four of the eight slots on the roadmap visual had been identified. The panel also confirmed a worldwide release for the Naruto Mobile game, which first launched in China in 2016.A release date for Naruto x Ninku has yet to be announced. Further details on Naruto Shadow Rising and the global rollout of Naruto Mobile are expected at Jump Festa 2027, taking place December 19 and 20.Read more at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Wasted Paris x Clarks Originals Pack Britpop Memorabilia Into a Customizable Wallabee Lite
Entertainment.text: Name: Wasted Paris x Clarks Wallabee LiteColorway: Black/BlackSKU: TBCMSRP: TBCRelease Date: October 15Where to Buy: WastedWasted Paris and Clarks Originals have teamed up on a Wallabee Lite in Black/Black that treats the shoe as a vessel for Britpop memorabilia. Built around a set of interchangeable pins, a guitar pick and a custom fob, the collaboration lets wearers decorate the silhouette themselves, mirroring the way fans of the era accumulated badges and souvenirs over time.The story begins in the mid-to-late ’90s, when the Wallabee became part of the Britpop landscape. The shoe turned up everywhere the scene gathered, from pubs and indie gigs to football terraces and backstage areas, along with every street that connected them. Britpop itself was never solely a sound. It was a mash-up of tastes, rituals, references and possessions that together formed the visual shorthand of a generation.Wasted Paris approaches that moment through memorabilia. Badges, charms, keepsakes and small personal touches pick up meaning the longer they’re kept, each one tied to a specific place, night or memory. The collaboration pulls from that same pool of era-defining imagery and everyday ephemera, and keeps it intentionally rough around the edges, favoring found fragments over anything too refined.That thinking is built directly into the shoe. The Wallabee Lite arrives fully blacked out, with a custom vamp carrying a tonal lion graphic and a co-branded fob that hangs from the laces. Interchangeable pins can be clipped onto the upper in any arrangement, alongside a guitar pick, so no two pairs need to look the same. A set of extra laces in contrasting blue rounds out the kit for further personalization.The packaging doubles as part of the collectible. Economy & Markets.title: Starbucks Reportedly Wants to Buy Chipotle in a Nearly $39 Billion USD Deal
Economy & Markets.text: SummaryStarbucks has reportedly been working with advisers on a possible proposal to acquire Chipotle Mexican GrillThe coffee giant’s market value is close to triple Chipotle’s, though analysts warn a deal could strain its finances mid-turnaroundNeither company has confirmed the talks, and it is unclear whether a formal offer will followStarbucks is reportedly exploring a takeover of Chipotle Mexican Grill, according to the Financial Times. The coffee chain has spent recent months consulting advisers on a potential proposal for the fast-casual brand, which carries a valuation of nearly $39 billion USD. Neither company has publicly addressed the reported discussions.On paper, the size gap is significant. Starbucks holds a market capitalization of roughly $107 billion USD, making it around 2.7 times larger than its potential target. Even so, swallowing a company of Chipotle’s scale would not come cheap, and financing is already emerging as the central question. “A deal could require heavy borrowing or issuing shares,” said Lale Akoner, global market strategist at eToro. “Without a compelling financial case, investors may view the deal as an expensive distraction.”The footprint numbers tell a different story. Chipotle closed out 2025 with close to 4,000 restaurants in the US and only about 100 abroad, while Starbucks operates approximately 40,000 stores globally. That imbalance is the core of the bullish case. Northcoast Research analyst Jim Sanderson pointed to Starbucks’ licensed partnerships in Europe as a potential launchpad for pushing Chipotle overseas at a much faster clip.Markets reacted quickly. Chipotle stock rose about 6% on Thursday, October 8, after the report surfaced, while Starbucks shares slipped roughly 3%. The bump offers some relief for Chipotle, whose share price has fallen by almost half since Niccol exited in 2024, a stretch marked by softer foot traffic and climbing food and labor costs.Starbucks’ own metrics show a turnaround still in progress. Niccol took over as CEO in September 2024 after six years at the helm of Chipotle, where he steered the brand through its food safety fallout and built out its digital ordering arm. At Starbucks, his strategy has centered on shorter waits, better staffing and refreshed stores, backed by a labor commitment of at least $500 million USD that has weighed on margins. The company has now posted four straight quarters of comparable sales growth, though Niccol conceded in July that the job is not yet done.For now, the numbers remain hypothetical. Both chains are contending with higher operating expenses and more cautious consumer spending, and until either side confirms the talks or a formal offer materializes, the deal exists only as a report.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast
